svg.title: AWS IAM
svg.desc: AWS IAM. Who may do what in AWS: principals, policies and roles that hand out temporary credentials, and how a request is evaluated. Step 1, Where it sits: Calls to AWS are signed with credentials (SigV4) and checked by IAM: people, functions and CI alike. Step 2, Temporary credentials: Lambda assumes thumbnailer-role; STS returns keys that expire; the SDK signs each S3 call with them. Step 3, Evaluating a request: An explicit Deny anywhere wins; without one, the call needs an Allow, or it is implicitly denied. Step 4, Least privilege, limits: Tighten with Access Analyzer and CloudTrail; mind size quotas, propagation and long-lived keys.

g.text: Calls to AWS are signed with credentials (SigV4) and checked by IAM: people, functions and CI alike.
Lambda assumes thumbnailer-role; STS returns keys that expire; the SDK signs each S3 call with them.
An explicit Deny anywhere wins; without one, the call needs an Allow, or it is implicitly denied.
Tighten with Access Analyzer and CloudTrail; mind size quotas, propagation and long-lived keys.
no key in code or image
EVERY CALL IS SIGNED, THEN AUTHORIZED
People sign in through IAM Identity Center with MFA and work in the role their permission set provides. Workloads use roles: Lambda
execution roles, ECS task roles, EC2 instance profiles. CI trades an OIDC token for a role; other accounts assume cross-account roles.
Requests carry a SigV4 signature. IAM checks it, then the policies: anything that no policy allows is denied (the root user aside).
Trust policy: who may assume it, here lambda.amazonaws.com.
Permissions policy: what its sessions may do in photos-prod.
Lambda assumes it for you: nothing secret in code or image.
STS returns an AccessKeyId (ASIA…), secret, session token, expiry.
Lambda exposes them as AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID … AWS_SESSION_TOKEN.
The SDK signs with SigV4 and sends X-Amz-Security-Token along.
An explicit Deny in any policy ends it: denied, whatever allows.
Otherwise SCPs and RCPs, an identity or resource policy, and any
boundary or session policy must all allow it; if not, implicit deny.
DeleteObject: 403, no identity-based policy allows the action.
http GetObject: 403, explicit deny in a resource-based policy.
S3 adds this context for callers in the same account or org.
Start narrow. Access Analyzer drafts a policy from up to 90 days
of CloudTrail (S3 object calls are data events: service only) and
flags unused roles, keys, passwords and actions, for a monthly fee.
LONG-LIVED KEYS AND THE ROOT USER
An access key (AKIA…) works until it is deactivated or deleted.
Prefer roles and federation, MFA for people, and the root user
only for the few tasks that need it.
